diff --git a/inflection/__init__.py b/inflection/__init__.py
index ffac5ce22e60816f18267d742455e4936b6d1c1a..1f3a5eae9baa00bfb8f7b597f737a265cdfca100 100644
--- a/inflection/__init__.py
+++ b/inflection/__init__.py
@@ -370,13 +370,40 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
       'The Man Without A Past'
       >>> titleize("raiders_of_the_lost_ark")
       'Raiders Of The Lost Ark'
+      >>> titleize("read the HTTP spec")
+      'Read The HTTP Spec'
+      >>> titleize("HELLO WORLD")
+      'Hello World'
+
+    All-caps acronyms are kept as they are, but only when the input also
+    contains lowercase letters; a fully uppercase input is titleized normally.
 
     """
-    return re.sub(
+    acronyms = []
+    if re.search(r"[a-z]", word):
+        def protect(match):
+            acronyms.append(match.group(0))
+            return chr(_ACRONYM_PLACEHOLDER_BASE + len(acronyms) - 1)
+
+        word = _ACRONYM_RE.sub(protect, word)
+
+    result = re.sub(
         r"\b('?\w)",
         lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
         humanize(underscore(word)).title()
     )
+    return re.sub(
+        r"[-]",
+        lambda match: acronyms[ord(match.group(0)) - _ACRONYM_PLACEHOLDER_BASE],
+        result,
+    )
+
+
+# An all-caps word (optionally with digits) that contains a capital letter and
+# is not glued to other letters or digits, e.g. "NASA" or "HTTP2".
+_ACRONYM_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z\d])(?=[A-Z\d]*[A-Z])[A-Z\d]{2,}(?![A-Za-z\d])")
+# Private-use code points standing in for acronyms while titleize runs.
+_ACRONYM_PLACEHOLDER_BASE = 0xE000
